This role combines content strategy, copywriting, content planning, and community management to create engaging campaigns that strengthen brand awareness and drive audience growth. Part of our Marketing team, you will develop content strategies, manage publishing calendars, craft compelling messaging, and ensure a consistent brand voice across all social media platforms. This role is ideal for someone who understands what content resonates with different audiences, stays on top of social media trends, and uses performance insights to continuously improve results. Key Responsibilities Develop and execute social media content strategies that align with brand objectives and marketing campaigns across multiple brands. Create engaging, platform-specific copy and messaging for LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and other digital channels. Plan and manage content calendars, ensuring a consistent and strategic publishing schedule across all social media platforms. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to produce high-quality creative content that reflects the brand's identity and goals. Identify emerging social media trends, formats, and cultural moments to create timely and relevant content that increases engagement and audience growth. Ensure consistency in brand voice, tone, and messaging across all customer-facing content. Manage day-to-day social media activity, including scheduling posts, monitoring channels, and responding to comments, messages, and community interactions in a timely and professional manner. Support the development of campaign concepts, content briefs, and creative direction for marketing initiatives. Monitor social media performance, audience engagement, and campaign effectiveness, providing regular reports and actionable recommendations to optimize future content. Analyze content performance and creative asset effectiveness using platform analytics and data-driven insights to continuously improve results. Stay informed on industry best practices, competitor activity, and evolving platform features to identify new opportunities for brand growth. Experience developing content calendars and managing social media publishing schedules. Proven experience creating social media strategies that drive audience growth, engagement, and brand awareness. Strong understanding of major social media platforms, content trends, algorithms, and platform best practices. Experience using social media management and analytics tools (e.g., Meta Business Suite, LinkedIn Analytics, Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Buffer, or similar). Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

Safe and Accountable Programming Initiatives Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in the development of guidance to support country teams to establish/improve community-based communication plans to ensure systematic information sharing/communication with affected communities throughout the programming cycle, ensuring that affected populations can make informed decisions about the assistance they receive and be able to hold humanitarian actors to account from programmatic commitments, the expected behavior of humanitarian actors, and rights and entitlements inherent in humanitarian action. Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in the development of information sharing/communications plans and tools for disseminating messages to crisis-affected communities in simple, easily understood terms, and accessible and preferred languages and formats. Participate in routine solicitation and collection of beneficiary feedback regarding IMC’s activities and stated commitments. Support programs and operations to adopt approaches to ensure protection mainstreaming. Project Design and Planning Support country offices to conduct protection risk assessments for affected populations, ensuring that program teams properly identify risks and generate mitigating measures, and to maintain an updated Protection Mainstreaming Action Plan. Support the completion of complementary AAP analysis/assessments, including, but not limited to stakeholder analysis, communication needs assessment, and community consultations. Project Implementation Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in ensuring that AAP data is collected routinely throughout the project cycle (not just at project mid and endpoints, enabling corrective action). Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in ensuring tools and systems are in place for learning and decision making on the needs of crisis-affected groups, including disaggregation of all data, development of mainstream and specific indicators, specific research questions, and targeted recommendations in reports. Community Based Feedback and Response Mechanism Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in maintaining local CBFRM, a systematic process to capture, monitor, resolve, and respond to feedback and complaints from crisis-affected communities. Support the A/E Manager and A/E Officer with the implementation of methodologies to consult communities on their preferences based on the operational context. Facilitate the solicitation and receipt of beneficiary feedback on the quality of IMC programs through dedicated channels and raise awareness of the channels among fellow staff and within the communities with which IMC works. Receive feedback regularly from field offices through various channels (feedback boxes, WhatsApp, email/phone hotline, help desks, etc.) and enter data promptly into the central CBFRM database. Support A/E Officer in processing all feedback/complaints and following up with relevant departmental focal persons to ensure that beneficiary complaints and feedback are properly addressed. Support A/E Officer to ensure that complaints are systematically responded to, explaining IMC actions/decisions to resolve issues are communicated back to the individual/community who raised them. Provide A/E Officer with reports on the status of the feedback system, caseload, and recommendations. Data management systems Enter data promptly and accurately into the CBFRM central database. Ensure central CBFRM database is maintained, and data is analyzed for trends and disseminating findings. Perform other duties as assigned. review_candidates.title: HR Legal & Compliance Expert
review_candidates.description: We Are Hiring : HR Legal & Compliance Expert Department : Human Resources Reports To : Human Resources Manager Work Location: Head Office – Tripoli, with regular coverage of the Benghazi branch (travel as required) Employment Type : Full-time, Permanent Contract (subject to the legally prescribed probation period) Grade / Level : Senior Specialist (in accordance with the Human Resources Career Path Framework) Purpose of the Role Presto is Libya’s leading food and grocery delivery platform, with a large and rapidly growing workforce across Tripoli and Benghazi. As the company continues to expand, the volume of employee-related cases — including disciplinary violations, complaints and grievances, disputes over salaries and deductions, absenteeism, contractual breaches, and end-of-service disputes — has grown beyond what the Human Resources team can effectively manage through informal or ad hoc processes. Every unresolved case carries potential legal and financial risks for the company. The Legal Affairs & Compliance Expert role is established to take full ownership of this area from beginning to end. The primary responsibility of the role is to manage both the existing backlog and the daily flow of employee-related cases, investigate them thoroughly, resolve them accurately and promptly, and ensure that every employment-related decision made by the company is legally defensible under Libyan law — particularly Labour Relations Law No. 12 of 2010 , its Executive Regulations, and other relevant legislation. The second responsibility is preventive in nature: to review and improve the contracts, policies, and procedures that contribute to recurring employee issues, with the objective of reducing the volume of cases over time. This is a hands-on execution role in which the job holder is expected to manage cases directly, rather than serve solely in an advisory capacity. Performance will be measured based on the number of cases successfully closed, disputes prevented, and audit findings resolved. Key Responsibilities A. Employee Relations, Case Resolution & Dispute Management (Primary Responsibility — approximately 50% of time) Case Management. Own and manage the company’s employee relations case register. Triage all incoming cases—including misconduct, complaints, grievances, payroll disputes, absenteeism and job abandonment, allegations, and other employee conduct issues—based on severity and legal risk, and lead each case through to closure within the service levels defined under the company’s Disciplinary and Grievance Policy. Investigations. Lead or oversee workplace investigations, including evidence gathering, interviewing employees and witnesses, hearing the employee’s response or defence, documenting findings, and preparing written investigation reports with reasoned recommendations. Lawful Disciplinary Action. Ensure that every disciplinary measure—from a written warning through to termination—is applied in accordance with the disciplinary scale set out in company policy, complies with notification, hearing, and procedural time-limit requirements under the Libyan Labour Relations Law and its Executive Regulations, and is properly documented before any final decision is issued. Employee Entitlement Disputes. Resolve disputes relating to salaries, allowances, deductions, overtime, leave balances, and end-of-service entitlements in coordination with Payroll and Finance, ensuring that all amounts are correctly calculated in accordance with applicable law and the approved salary structure. Mediation. Act as the first point of mediation between employees and their direct managers, seeking amicable settlement before escalation, and prepare settlement agreements and final release documents where appropriate. External Dispute Management. Represent the company, or guide and provide information to external legal counsel, in matters before the Labour Office, conciliation committees, and labour courts. Prepare the company’s case file, evidence, and legal position for each dispute. Backlog Resolution. Clear the backlog of open employee cases within the first 90 days and submit a weekly report to the HR Manager covering case status, ageing, progress, and legal risk. B. Legal Compliance & Risk Control (Approximately 25% of time) Legal Knowledge and Monitoring. Maintain an up-to-date compliance map of the company’s obligations under labour, social security, occupational health and safety, and related legislation. Monitor new laws, regulations, and ministerial decisions affecting the workforce. Employment Contracts. Review all employment and engagement contracts—including full-time, part-time, internship, and service contracts, including arrangements for cleaners and warehouse workers—to ensure compliance with legal requirements and standardize all templates. Terms and Conditions of Employment. Verify that working hours, rest periods, overtime, weekly rest, public holidays, annual leave, sick leave, maternity leave, probation periods, notice periods, and end-of-service entitlements are applied in accordance with the law across all branches and shifts. Social Security. Ensure employees are properly registered with the Social Security Fund, contributions are accurate, workplace injuries are reported, and all related declarations and submissions are completed on time, in coordination with Payroll. Registrations and Permits. Ensure that the company’s labour-related registrations remain complete and valid, including approval of the Internal Work Regulations, internship and trainee arrangements, foreign worker permits, and required filings with the Labour Office. Audits and Reporting. Conduct quarterly HR compliance audits, maintain a risk register with assigned owners and deadlines, and escalate material risks to the HR Manager and Executive Management. C. Policies, Procedures & Internal Regulations (Approximately 15% of time) Policies. Draft, review, and update the company’s Internal Work Regulations, Disciplinary and Grievance Policy, Code of Conduct, attendance and leave rules, and other HR policies to ensure they are legally compliant, clear, practical, and enforceable. Manage their approval by the relevant authority where required. Procedures and Templates. Design and document a standard operating procedure for each type of employee relations case, including investigation steps, forms, hearing minutes, decision letters, and appeal processes, ensuring consistent application by HR staff and managers. Root-Cause Analysis. Analyse patterns of recurring employee issues by branch, department, manager, or issue type, and recommend root-cause solutions—such as training, process changes, contractual amendments, or recruitment improvements—to reduce the volume of cases. D. Advisory, Training & Organisational Culture (Approximately 10% of time) Advisory Support. Provide clear, practical legal advice to the HR team, department managers, and senior management before decisions are taken regarding recruitment, restructuring, transfers, salary adjustments, termination of employment, redundancies, and workforce reductions. Training. Train managers and supervisors on lawful disciplinary practices, proper documentation, grievance handling, and the avoidance of common legal mistakes. Deliver induction and awareness sessions for newly appointed managers. Organisational Culture. Promote a fair, transparent, and consistent employee relations culture in which employees trust the grievance process and managers consistently comply with company rules and procedures. 4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) The job holder’s performance will be evaluated based on a set of key performance indicators, including: Case Closure Within Service Levels: Achieve a minimum of 85% of cases closed within the specified timeframe , based on their severity and the violations and complaints policy. Average Case Age: Reduce the average number of days from case opening to closure, with a continuous quarter-over-quarter reduction . Soundness of Disciplinary Decisions: Achieve a minimum of 90% of disciplinary decisions upheld during internal appeals or before the relevant external authorities. Reduction of External Disputes: Continuously reduce the number of cases escalated to the Labor Office or courts, while ensuring no case is lost due to a procedural error . Audit Findings Compliance: Maintain zero high-risk audit findings that exceed their remediation deadlines during quarterly audits. Employment Contract Compliance: Ensure that 100% of active employees have signed employment contracts that comply with applicable laws and regulations. Social Security Compliance: Ensure that 100% of eligible employees are registered and that contributions are paid on time. Manager Training: Train at least 90% of managers during the first year on lawful disciplinary procedures, complaint management, and the proper handling of employee-related cases. Reduction in Case Recurrence: Maintain the rate of cases reopened or recurring with the same employee or manager within six months at 10% or below . 5. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Law from a recognized university. Membership in the Libyan Bar Association, or eligibility for membership, is preferred. At least 3 years of experience in labor law and employee relations, including at least one year of experience in Human Resources or Legal Affairs. Knowledge of Labor Relations Law No. (12) of 2010, the Social Security Law, and the procedures of labor offices and labor courts. Experience in disciplinary investigations, complaints, labor and financial disputes, and their legal resolution. Experience in preparing and managing cases for settlement or litigation. Experience in drafting and reviewing employment contracts, internal regulations, and company policies. Proficiency in Arabic, legal drafting, and report preparation.

new_matches.title: Assistant, Accountability and Effectiveness
new_matches.description: JOB SUMMARY: The Accountability and Effectiveness (A/E) Assistant supports the A/E team to ensure accountability mechanisms are in place at the country level, and that they are being implemented across all programs to fulfill IMC’s minimum accountability standards, especially regarding community engagement (including information sharing, beneficiaries’ meaningful participation, and feedback and complaints handling). This position also supports the A/E team to ensure protection mainstreaming mechanisms are implemented across all programs, ensuring that IMC programs are safe, effective, and accountable, and that these programs adhere to the four main principles of Protection Mainstreaming in all programs. With the support of the A/E Officer, the Assistant will be the primary person responsible for collecting and documenting feedback and complaints received through the country Community Based Feedback and Response Mechanisms (CBFRM). Additionally, this position will provide daily/weekly/monthly reporting on feedback and complaints and analysis on the utilization of various channels to their supervisor. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation. Main Tasks And Responsibilities Policies, Guidance, and Procedures Support the A/E Manager and A/E Officer for reporting on AAP and CHS commitments. Contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of the Code of Conduct, humanitarian principles, and the 9 Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) commitments. Safe and Accountable Programming Initiatives Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in the development of guidance to support country teams to establish/improve community-based communication plans to ensure systematic information sharing/communication with affected communities throughout the programming cycle, ensuring that affected populations can make informed decisions about the assistance they receive and be able to hold humanitarian actors to account from programmatic commitments, the expected behavior of humanitarian actors, and rights and entitlements inherent in humanitarian action. Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in the development of information sharing/communications plans and tools for disseminating messages to crisis-affected communities in simple, easily understood terms, and accessible and preferred languages and formats. Participate in routine solicitation and collection of beneficiary feedback regarding IMC’s activities and stated commitments. Support programs and operations to adopt approaches to ensure protection mainstreaming. Project Design and Planning Support country offices to conduct protection risk assessments for affected populations, ensuring that program teams properly identify risks and generate mitigating measures, and to maintain an updated Protection Mainstreaming Action Plan. Support the completion of complementary AAP analysis/assessments, including, but not limited to stakeholder analysis, communication needs assessment, and community consultations. Project Implementation Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in ensuring that AAP data is collected routinely throughout the project cycle (not just at project mid and endpoints, enabling corrective action). Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in ensuring tools and systems are in place for learning and decision making on the needs of crisis-affected groups, including disaggregation of all data, development of mainstream and specific indicators, specific research questions, and targeted recommendations in reports. Community Based Feedback and Response Mechanism Support A/E Manager and A/E Officer in maintaining local CBFRM, a systematic process to capture, monitor, resolve, and respond to feedback and complaints from crisis-affected communities. Support the A/E Manager and A/E Officer with the implementation of methodologies to consult communities on their preferences based on the operational context. Facilitate the solicitation and receipt of beneficiary feedback on the quality of IMC programs through dedicated channels and raise awareness of the channels among fellow staff and within the communities with which IMC works. Receive feedback regularly from field offices through various channels (feedback boxes, WhatsApp, email/phone hotline, help desks, etc.) and enter data promptly into the central CBFRM database. Assist in conducting field visits as necessary to monitor data collection and ensure proper placement of suggestion boxes and signage in supported facilities. Support A/E Officer in maintaining and updating the CBFRM database, tracking all feedback and complaints from point of receipt through closure. Support A/E Officer in reviewing, categorizing, and referring feedback to relevant internal departments and external service providers. Support A/E Officer in processing all feedback/complaints and following up with relevant departmental focal persons to ensure that beneficiary complaints and feedback are properly addressed. Support A/E Officer to ensure that complaints are systematically responded to, explaining IMC actions/decisions to resolve issues are communicated back to the individual/community who raised them. Provide A/E Officer with reports on the status of the feedback system, caseload, and recommendations. Data management systems Enter data promptly and accurately into the CBFRM central database. Ensure central CBFRM database is maintained, and data is analyzed for trends and disseminating findings. Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive. Minimum Qualifications Typically, a diploma in social sciences, public health, statistics, or international development, with experience or background in accountability to affected population, protection mainstreaming, and/or safeguarding. An equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate. Typically, a minimum of 2+ years of applied experience with a humanitarian organization and working with refugees/IDPs in humanitarian settings. Demonstrated basic knowledge of accountability mechanisms. Demonstrated strong experience with database entry and management. Excellent understanding of the local context. Personal and organizational skills, including time management and the ability to meet deadlines. Ability to follow up with different departments. Should be highly computer literate, with a good level of proficiency in Microsoft Office applications including Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook. Effective communicator, active learner, team player, and able to work effectively with people from various groups and backgrounds. Demonstrated understanding of data collection methods. Medium-level English proficiency (Speaking – Reading – Writing) High-level COUNTRY-SPECIFIC LANGUAGE proficiency (Speaking – Reading – Writing).

new_matches.description: We Are Hiring : HR Legal & Compliance Expert Department : Human Resources Reports To : Human Resources Manager Work Location: Head Office – Tripoli, with regular coverage of the Benghazi branch (travel as required) Employment Type : Full-time, Permanent Contract (subject to the legally prescribed probation period) Grade / Level : Senior Specialist (in accordance with the Human Resources Career Path Framework) Purpose of the Role Presto is Libya’s leading food and grocery delivery platform, with a large and rapidly growing workforce across Tripoli and Benghazi. As the company continues to expand, the volume of employee-related cases — including disciplinary violations, complaints and grievances, disputes over salaries and deductions, absenteeism, contractual breaches, and end-of-service disputes — has grown beyond what the Human Resources team can effectively manage through informal or ad hoc processes. Every unresolved case carries potential legal and financial risks for the company. The Legal Affairs & Compliance Expert role is established to take full ownership of this area from beginning to end. The primary responsibility of the role is to manage both the existing backlog and the daily flow of employee-related cases, investigate them thoroughly, resolve them accurately and promptly, and ensure that every employment-related decision made by the company is legally defensible under Libyan law — particularly Labour Relations Law No. 12 of 2010 , its Executive Regulations, and other relevant legislation. The second responsibility is preventive in nature: to review and improve the contracts, policies, and procedures that contribute to recurring employee issues, with the objective of reducing the volume of cases over time. This is a hands-on execution role in which the job holder is expected to manage cases directly, rather than serve solely in an advisory capacity. Performance will be measured based on the number of cases successfully closed, disputes prevented, and audit findings resolved. Key Responsibilities A. Employee Relations, Case Resolution & Dispute Management (Primary Responsibility — approximately 50% of time) Case Management. Own and manage the company’s employee relations case register. Triage all incoming cases—including misconduct, complaints, grievances, payroll disputes, absenteeism and job abandonment, allegations, and other employee conduct issues—based on severity and legal risk, and lead each case through to closure within the service levels defined under the company’s Disciplinary and Grievance Policy. Investigations. Lead or oversee workplace investigations, including evidence gathering, interviewing employees and witnesses, hearing the employee’s response or defence, documenting findings, and preparing written investigation reports with reasoned recommendations. Lawful Disciplinary Action. Ensure that every disciplinary measure—from a written warning through to termination—is applied in accordance with the disciplinary scale set out in company policy, complies with notification, hearing, and procedural time-limit requirements under the Libyan Labour Relations Law and its Executive Regulations, and is properly documented before any final decision is issued. Employee Entitlement Disputes. Resolve disputes relating to salaries, allowances, deductions, overtime, leave balances, and end-of-service entitlements in coordination with Payroll and Finance, ensuring that all amounts are correctly calculated in accordance with applicable law and the approved salary structure. Mediation. Act as the first point of mediation between employees and their direct managers, seeking amicable settlement before escalation, and prepare settlement agreements and final release documents where appropriate. External Dispute Management. Represent the company, or guide and provide information to external legal counsel, in matters before the Labour Office, conciliation committees, and labour courts. Prepare the company’s case file, evidence, and legal position for each dispute. Backlog Resolution. Clear the backlog of open employee cases within the first 90 days and submit a weekly report to the HR Manager covering case status, ageing, progress, and legal risk. B. Legal Compliance & Risk Control (Approximately 25% of time) Legal Knowledge and Monitoring. Maintain an up-to-date compliance map of the company’s obligations under labour, social security, occupational health and safety, and related legislation. Monitor new laws, regulations, and ministerial decisions affecting the workforce. Employment Contracts. Review all employment and engagement contracts—including full-time, part-time, internship, and service contracts, including arrangements for cleaners and warehouse workers—to ensure compliance with legal requirements and standardize all templates. Terms and Conditions of Employment. Verify that working hours, rest periods, overtime, weekly rest, public holidays, annual leave, sick leave, maternity leave, probation periods, notice periods, and end-of-service entitlements are applied in accordance with the law across all branches and shifts. Social Security. Ensure employees are properly registered with the Social Security Fund, contributions are accurate, workplace injuries are reported, and all related declarations and submissions are completed on time, in coordination with Payroll. Registrations and Permits. Ensure that the company’s labour-related registrations remain complete and valid, including approval of the Internal Work Regulations, internship and trainee arrangements, foreign worker permits, and required filings with the Labour Office. Audits and Reporting. Conduct quarterly HR compliance audits, maintain a risk register with assigned owners and deadlines, and escalate material risks to the HR Manager and Executive Management. C. Policies, Procedures & Internal Regulations (Approximately 15% of time) Policies. Draft, review, and update the company’s Internal Work Regulations, Disciplinary and Grievance Policy, Code of Conduct, attendance and leave rules, and other HR policies to ensure they are legally compliant, clear, practical, and enforceable. Manage their approval by the relevant authority where required. Procedures and Templates. Design and document a standard operating procedure for each type of employee relations case, including investigation steps, forms, hearing minutes, decision letters, and appeal processes, ensuring consistent application by HR staff and managers. Root-Cause Analysis. Analyse patterns of recurring employee issues by branch, department, manager, or issue type, and recommend root-cause solutions—such as training, process changes, contractual amendments, or recruitment improvements—to reduce the volume of cases. D. Advisory, Training & Organisational Culture (Approximately 10% of time) Advisory Support. Provide clear, practical legal advice to the HR team, department managers, and senior management before decisions are taken regarding recruitment, restructuring, transfers, salary adjustments, termination of employment, redundancies, and workforce reductions. Training. Train managers and supervisors on lawful disciplinary practices, proper documentation, grievance handling, and the avoidance of common legal mistakes. Deliver induction and awareness sessions for newly appointed managers. Organisational Culture. Promote a fair, transparent, and consistent employee relations culture in which employees trust the grievance process and managers consistently comply with company rules and procedures. 4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) The job holder’s performance will be evaluated based on a set of key performance indicators, including: Case Closure Within Service Levels: Achieve a minimum of 85% of cases closed within the specified timeframe , based on their severity and the violations and complaints policy. Average Case Age: Reduce the average number of days from case opening to closure, with a continuous quarter-over-quarter reduction . Soundness of Disciplinary Decisions: Achieve a minimum of 90% of disciplinary decisions upheld during internal appeals or before the relevant external authorities. Reduction of External Disputes: Continuously reduce the number of cases escalated to the Labor Office or courts, while ensuring no case is lost due to a procedural error . Audit Findings Compliance: Maintain zero high-risk audit findings that exceed their remediation deadlines during quarterly audits. Employment Contract Compliance: Ensure that 100% of active employees have signed employment contracts that comply with applicable laws and regulations. Social Security Compliance: Ensure that 100% of eligible employees are registered and that contributions are paid on time. Manager Training: Train at least 90% of managers during the first year on lawful disciplinary procedures, complaint management, and the proper handling of employee-related cases. Reduction in Case Recurrence: Maintain the rate of cases reopened or recurring with the same employee or manager within six months at 10% or below . 5. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Law from a recognized university. Membership in the Libyan Bar Association, or eligibility for membership, is preferred. At least 3 years of experience in labor law and employee relations, including at least one year of experience in Human Resources or Legal Affairs. Knowledge of Labor Relations Law No. (12) of 2010, the Social Security Law, and the procedures of labor offices and labor courts. Experience in disciplinary investigations, complaints, labor and financial disputes, and their legal resolution. Experience in preparing and managing cases for settlement or litigation. Experience in drafting and reviewing employment contracts, internal regulations, and company policies. Proficiency in Arabic, legal drafting, and report preparation.

Revenue Cycle Management • Oversee revenue cycle functions, including Medicaid and private-pay billing, collections, and reimbursement processes, ensuring timely and accurate revenue recognition. • Direct claims denial management, appeals processes, and resolution of billing discrepancies. • Monitor key revenue cycle metrics, including days in accounts receivable, collection rates, and payer mix. • Prepare and submit Medicaid Waiver Cost Reports to DHHS Division of Health Benefits and the Office of the Controller. • Maintain financial practices consistent with HIPA Financial Systems, Technology, Compliance, and Reporting • Manage the relationship with the audit firm(s) for the audit of the annual financial statements and 401(k) plan. • Leverage ASNC’s core financial technology stack — NetSuite (ERP), Paycom (payroll/HR), and Power BI (business intelligence and reporting) — to drive automation, data integrity, and real- time financial visibility. • Serve as 401(k) plan administrator/trustee and member of the 401(k) Investment Committee, including filing Form 5500 for the 401(k) and Health and Welfare plans. • Compile cost and profit analysis, including requests for enhanced rates to Health Plans (commercial and Medicaid). • Manage cash accounts and endowment funds, including oversight and evaluation of investment managers and accounts. • Oversee grant and contract execution, reporting, business insurance, and employee benefits administration. • Ensure the integrity of financial statements and internal controls, and maintain compliance with GAAP, FASB nonprofit accounting standards, 2 CFR 200 (Uniform Guidance), and applicable federal, state, and grantor requirements. • Establish and enforce accounting and financial policies and procedures, ensuring alignment with state licensing and accreditation requirements. • Complete NC Personal Property tax returns and manage the tax exemption process for properties and vehicles.
